name: Non-FMA split product residual
definition: For binary64 operands a,b, let (a_h,a_l)=Split(a), (b_h,b_l)=Split(b), p=fl(ab), d_1=fl(p−fl(a_h b_h)), d_2=fl(d_1−fl(a_l b_h)), d_3=fl(d_2−fl(a_h b_l)), e=fl(fl(a_l b_l)−d_3); ab=p+e in real arithmetic on the stated domain.
variables: a,b operands; h and l high and low split components; p rounded product; d_j intermediate differences; e residual; fl rounds one operation
assumptions: IEEE binary64 round-to-nearest ties-to-even; registered Dekker split with factor 2^27+1; all operations separately rounded, no overflow or underflow in any nonzero intermediate, no reassociation or implicit FMA
limitations: The split itself can overflow even if ab is finite; the exact identity is restricted to this conservative arithmetic domain; additional scaling is outside the specification
failure_conditions: Nonfinite inputs or intermediate overflow or underflow
Arithmetic contraction, reassociation or unsupported rounding mode
computation: Split both operands using the registered significand-split recurrence, compute the rounded product and the three differences in the stated order, then subtract the last difference from the separately rounded low-component product.

source.citation: Ogita, Rump and Oishi (2005), Accurate Sum and Dot Product, p. 1961, Algorithm 3.3 and p. 1962, Theorem 3.4, DOI 10.1137/030601818. https://ogilab.w.waseda.jp/ogita/math/doc/2005_OgRuOi.pdf

application: General numerical product decomposition; no forecasting benefit claimed.
mechanism_note: Expanding (a_h+a_l)(b_h+b_l) shows the correction is ab−p; the paper establishes exactness of the ordered floating-point recurrence without underflow. Same output identity as the existing FMA transform, so classified as a variant rather than a new distinct algorithm.

name: Error-residual compensated dot product
definition: For n≥1, initialize (p_1,c_1)=TwoProduct(x_1,y_1); for i=2,…,n set (h_i,r_i)=TwoProduct(x_i,y_i), (p_i,q_i)=TwoSum(p_(i−1),h_i), c_i=fl(c_(i−1)+fl(q_i+r_i)); D=fl(p_n+c_n).
variables: x_i,y_i paired components; h_i rounded product; r_i multiplication residual; p_i running rounded sum; q_i addition residual; c_i rounded correction; D returned dot product
assumptions: Finite equal-length nonempty binary64 vectors; round-to-nearest ties-to-even, separate operations, no overflow or underflow in nonzero intermediates, and exact residual transforms on their declared domains; for the cited bound n u < 1 with unit roundoff u
limitations: Correction accumulation and final addition still round; cancellation may yield a large relative error; not guaranteed correctly rounded, exact, or superior on every input
failure_conditions: Unsupported residual arithmetic, overflow or underflow
Reassociation or implicit contraction of the specified operations
computation: Use the registered split product residual or FMA residual on its valid domain, and TwoSum for the running sum; accumulate both residual types in the stated order, returning the once-corrected rounded result.

source.citation: Ogita, Rump and Oishi (2005), Accurate Sum and Dot Product, pp. 1972–1973, Algorithms 5.3–5.4, equation (5.1), Proposition 5.5, DOI 10.1137/030601818. https://ogilab.w.waseda.jp/ogita/math/doc/2005_OgRuOi.pdf

application: General numerical inner-product computation; no forecasting benefit claimed.
required_inputs: Paired finite vectors and declared arithmetic
incompatible_methods: Inferring exact dot product from individual residuals
mechanism_note: With exact local transforms, q_i+r_i=x_i y_i+p_(i−1)−p_i. Telescoping yields xᵀy=p_n+c_1+Σ_(i=2)^n(q_i+r_i) before rounding the correction. Unlike compensated summation of already-rounded values, this mechanism also accounts for multiplication error; classified as a distinct inner-product algorithm.
